title: Melody Bus Run

selected_categories.reasoning: The player occupies one of exactly two lanes and the only gameplay input is switching lanes to line up with safe or rewarding objects.
The run auto-scrolls continuously, obstacles spawn indefinitely, the score is survival-based, and difficulty increases through speed rather than discrete stages.

Music, lyric callouts, synthesized melody scheduling, note collectibles, and singing-bus presentation are central to the game's identity, though input timing is not beat-matched in a strict rhythm-game sense.
The game strongly uses neon gradients, glowing UI, luminous road markings, and a stylized night-drive aesthetic that aligns with the neon runner category.
The challenge escalates mainly through rising speed and reflex pressure, but the structure is more survival score-chasing than race-against-time course completion.

uncertainty_notes: The game borrows heavily from rhythm/music presentation, but its interaction model is still closer to a simple lane-based endless runner than a true beat-timing game.
Neon runner is a good aesthetic fit rather than a stricter mechanical fit.
No category in the provided universe exactly captures a two-lane collectible-and-dodge runner with musical character performance, so the ranking balances mechanics first and presentation second.
